classification.classification_note: The benchmark metadata labels the sample CWE-787. The saved Stage 01 evidence is an AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow READ caused by using `strstr()` on a fixed-length stack buffer that is not NUL-terminated.

bug_description.original: Stack-buffer-overflow in is_http OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=504809218 ``` Crash type: Stack-buffer-overflow READ {*} Crash state: is_http stun_get_message_len_str FuzzStunClient.c ```
bug_description.normalized: The staged 8192-byte witness reaches `harness_channel_data()`, passes its `Size <= 8192` gate, and is copied byte-for-byte into a local `uint8_t buf[8192]`. Because the witness length exactly equals the stack buffer size and contains no `\0` byte anywhere in those 8192 copied bytes, the entire zero-initialized array is overwritten and no in-bounds string terminator remains. `stun_get_message_len_str()` then calls `is_http(buf, 8192)`. Vulnerable `is_http()` tests whether the buffer starts with `GET `, `POST `, `DELETE `, or `PUT ` by calling `strstr()` on `buf` as though it were a C string, ignoring the explicit `blen` bound. At least one unsuccessful prefix search therefore keeps scanning past `buf[8191]` into the adjacent stack redzone. Stage 01 reproduces `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8193` in `is_http`, and the patch fixes this exact obligation by replacing the unbounded `strstr()` prefix tests with the new length-aware `has_prefix(s, blen, ...)` helper.

source.description: First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant input state. This copy places the attacker bytes into the local stack buffer that later gets treated as a C string by `is_http()`.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/osv_ossfuzz_OSV-2026-608/poc` is exactly 8192 bytes (sha256 `7102206d9509b8773fd2e6d22d215a77fd3e697dc99dccf8c05a211890e05fd9`). `harness_channel_data()` admits that exact size, and because line 64 zero-initializes `uint8_t buf[8192]` before line 65 copies all 8192 attacker bytes, the copy overwrites the entire array and leaves no in-bounds NUL terminator. A direct scan of the saved witness shows `poc.count(b'\x00') == 0`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Unsafe memory read site in project code. Evaluating these `strstr()` prefix checks on the full 8192-byte non-NUL-terminated stack buffer causes libc to scan past `buf[8191]`, matching the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow read in `is_http()`.

root_cause.description: Missing bound-preserving prefix check. `is_http()` has an explicit buffer length parameter `blen`, but this branch ignores it and uses `strstr()` as if `s` were NUL-terminated. The fixing patch replaces this exact code with `has_prefix(s, blen, ...)` checks that stop at the provided extent.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant state is the exact copied stack buffer contents and extent. The attacker controls both the 8192 bytes copied into `buf` and the fact that the copy length equals the whole destination size, eliminating the zero fill that would otherwise terminate string searches in-bounds.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific admission gate for the crashing sub-harness. The saved witness size is exactly 8192, so it takes the accepted continuation and reaches the local `buf[8192]` copy used by `stun_get_message_len_str()`.
parser_admitted.condition: The witness must satisfy `4 <= Size <= 8192`; the staged PoC uses the upper boundary `Size == 8192`.

fine_trace.note: Reachability gate for the crashing harness path. The saved PoC length is exactly 8192, so this boundary check admits the input instead of returning early and allows the subsequent full-buffer stack copy.

Source step. `buf` was zero-initialized at line 64, but `Size == 8192` overwrites the entire `uint8_t buf[8192]` array with attacker bytes. The staged witness has no `\0` byte in those 8192 bytes, so the resulting stack buffer has no in-bounds C-string terminator.

The copied stack buffer is handed to the HTTP classifier as `(s = (char *)buf, blen = 8192)`. This is the parser-side transition from raw bytes to a bounded character buffer that `is_http()` will inspect.

The HTTP fast path is enabled because the copied buffer pointer is non-null and the admitted length is 8192, well above the 12-byte threshold. That control decision exposes the subsequent prefix tests to the full unterminated stack buffer.

Root cause. These prefix checks ignore the explicit `blen` bound and instead invoke `strstr()` on `s` as though it were NUL-terminated. The patch replaces this exact branch with `has_prefix(s, blen, ...)`, showing that the missing obligation is length-bounded prefix testing rather than searching an unbounded C string.

Sink. While evaluating these `strstr()` searches on the 8192-byte non-NUL-terminated stack buffer, libc reads past `buf[8191]` into the redzone after the array. Stage 01 captured `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow on address ... READ of size 8193` with crash stack `StrstrCheck -> strstr -> is_http -> stun_get_message_len_str -> harness_channel_data`.

format.name: exact 8192-byte non-NUL-terminated channel-data witness
format.contract: Exactly the staged 8192-byte witness stored at `gt_results/osv_ossfuzz_OSV-2026-608/poc` (sha256 `7102206d9509b8773fd2e6d22d215a77fd3e697dc99dccf8c05a211890e05fd9`). Verified properties of this saved file are: it satisfies the harness gate `4 <= Size <= 8192` at the upper boundary `Size == 8192`; it contains no `\0` byte anywhere in the copied 8192-byte extent; it begins with `PUT ` at offset 0; it also contains `GET ` at offset 6322; and it contains no `POST `, `DELETE `, ` HTTP/`, or `\r\n\r\n` substring in those 8192 bytes. Those exact witness properties ensure that vulnerable `is_http()` applies unbounded `strstr()` prefix searches to a full stack buffer with no in-bounds terminator, which is the verified trigger for the saved overread.
